Pattern Scanner — every timeframe, one coin

Wedges, double tops and bottoms, triangles, head & shoulders, flags · mechanically detected
Detection is mechanical; confirmation is not a forecast. Patterns are matched against one fixed geometric definition — swing pivots, least-squares trendlines, a tolerance you control. Confirmed means the breakout close has already happened, nothing more. Unlike the Open/Close Cross on the scanner page, these patterns have not been walk-forward tested in this toolkit, so no edge is claimed for them in either direction.
Pick a coin and press Scan.
Data: Binance public REST, USD-M futures (fapi.binance.com) or spot (api.binance.com). No key, no account. 13 timeframes; the six marked * are aggregated from 5m/1h/1d candles on exact epoch boundaries. The in-progress candle is always discarded, so nothing on this page repaints. Trendlines are least-squares fits through detected swing pivots — a different pivot width gives different lines, which is exactly why the width is an input and not a hidden constant.

Data: Binance USD-M futures public REST and WebSocket (fapi.binance.com, fstream.binance.com). No key, no account, nothing leaves your browser. Live liquidations are real executed force-orders from the !forceOrder@arr stream. Liquidation levels are computed, not observed — Binance publishes no map of where stops sit, and the per-tier maintenance margin table requires an API key, so a flat rate is assumed. Treat levels as arithmetic on an assumed average entry, not as known positions.

Volume Profile — where the coin actually traded

Volume by price, TPO / time at price, point of control, value area, naked POCs
Built from candles, not from every tick. Binance publishes no historical volume-at-price feed, so each candle's volume is spread across the prices it covered — the standard approximation. It resolves the shape of the profile, the point of control and the value area reliably; it will not match a tick-exact profile row for row. TPO counts candles touching a price, which is the same time-at-price idea a market profile is built on.

Session profiles

Pick a coin and press Build profile.
Data: Binance public REST, USD-M futures or spot. No key, no account. POC is the price row with the most volume (or most TPO). The value area is the narrowest band around the POC holding the chosen share of total activity — its edges are VAH and VAL. A naked POC is a past session's point of control that price has not traded back through since; they are listed because they are watched, not because they are proven. The in-progress candle is discarded, so nothing repaints.

Indicators — the whole panel, one coin

~45 indicators computed from live candles · classics plus the published community algorithms · nothing is fetched from TradingView
A count of agreeing indicators is not a probability. These are the standard formulas computed on closed candles — the readings are exact, the interpretation is the usual textbook one. This toolkit already measured what happens when many timeframes agree on one signal: the crowded buckets did worse than a random entry. A summary that says STRONG BUY means most formulas currently point up, and nothing more.
Pick a coin and press Read indicators.
Community algorithms are reimplemented from their published formulas — Squeeze Momentum and WaveTrend (LazyBear), SuperTrend (KivancOzbilgic), UT Bot (QuantNomad), Williams Vix Fix (ChrisMoody), supply/demand zones with BOS from FluidTrades' SMC Lite (Pmgjiv, MPL-2.0), and the standard smart-money building blocks (swing structure, fair value gaps). No Pine source is fetched, copied or executed; closed-source scripts cannot be reproduced at all. Values will track those indicators closely but will not always match a specific author's variant parameter for parameter.

Strategies — 56 rule sets, backtested on live candles

Every classic entry rule plus the published community ones, run over real history with fees, on the coin and timeframe you choose
This is an in-sample fit, and that is the whole problem. Every row below is one rule scored on one coin over one window it has already seen. The scanner's own signal looked like +0.18% per trade under exactly this kind of scoring, then delivered −1.06% walk-forward with 0 of 4 folds positive. Ranking 48 rules and taking the top one is the fastest way to reproduce that mistake. Read the table as a description of the past, and re-test anything promising on a window it has never touched.
Pick a coin and press Backtest all.
Execution model: a rule reads only closed candles up to bar i, and the resulting position is held through bar i+1 — no signal is ever acted on inside the bar that produced it, so nothing here is lookahead. Equity is marked to market every bar. The round-trip fee is charged as half on entry and half on exit, and a flip from long to short pays both. Community rules are reimplemented from their published formulas; no Pine source is fetched or executed.

Timeframe ladder — where every band sits, and which one is next to go

The band's colour is not the signal; its distance from the candle is. 30m can be short while 45m is still long simply because the 45m band is further away — price has not reached it yet. The same reason makes 4h and 1d structurally late: their band can sit 10% below, so they keep printing LONG long after the move turned. This reads every timeframe from 5 minutes to 1 week and shows, for each one, the two band prices (those are your support and resistance), how far the candle is from them, and how far price must travel for that timeframe to flip.
Distance is measured in ATR of that timeframe, never in percent — 1% on the 5-minute chart and 1% on the daily are not the same distance, and matching in percent instead of ATR is the error that made a whole family of zone results look real when they were not. A band the candle is sitting on is marked WEAK: price cuts through it. The entry is the nearest band that is far enough away to still mean something.

Spot signals — what every rule says about your coins right now

Spot signals. What every rule in the research set says about your spot coins right now, read on closed daily candles. Two groups, kept apart on purpose because they disagree and the disagreement is the point: trend rules (the two that passed six out of six windows) and stretch rules (overbought / far from average / new high — the ones people actually sell on). Each row carries its own measured record, so you can see which reading is worth acting on before you act on it.
Press Read signals — it reads ★ My list on closed candles.

Spot rebalance — the one spot rule that beat holding

Spot — rebalancing, not timing. Selling to buy back lower was tested and rejected: a random sell date beat every signal, and compounding 608 round trips left 0.2% of the stack. Rebalancing was the opposite — on your own basket, trimming winners into losers every 90 days turned 2.15× into 3.36× over 3.4 years with 13 trades and under 1% in fees. It never predicts anything; it sells what grew and buys what fell. This page tells you the trades — it places nothing, because your spot coins are not in the paper account.
Press Check my weights — it reads ★ My list and the live prices.
Watches your coins on every timeframe you tick and opens paper trades by itself. Every round it reads each coin on each timeframe, and when the OCC crosses on the candle that just closed it opens a paper position in this toolkit's paper account — LONG on a cross up, SHORT on a cross down — closing the opposite one it holds for that coin and timeframe. It watches whichever coins the Coins picker at the top of the page is set to, and uses the MA type and Alt res × from there too. It only runs while this page is open. Paper only: no real order is ever sent.

Signals coming from TradingView. On a free TradingView plan there is no webhook, so copy the alert text (from the alert pop-up, the Alerts log, or the alert e-mail) and paste it below — one alert per line, as many as you like. It understands this script's alerts, for example OCC HTF LONG BTCUSDT @ 81000 or WEEKLY OVERSOLD ETHUSDT RSI 28, and most other "SYMBOL LONG/SHORT price" texts. If you later get a paid plan, point the alert webhook at http://<this computer>:8080/tv-webhook?token=YOURSECRET and signals land here by themselves. For that the server has to be started open to the network with a token — serve.ps1 8080 -Bind 0.0.0.0 -Token YOURSECRET — because by default it listens on this machine only and answers webhooks from nowhere else.

Long-term support = where the 200-week average, past yearly lows and monthly swing lows stack up. Mid-term support = the 50-week average, weekly swing lows and the 3-month low. The strongest zone is the one with the most levels stacked together and the most past bounces. BUY = a weekly candle closed inside the zone and bounced (green close or weekly RSI ≤ 35). No support is guaranteed: every plan has a stop under the zone, and the History columns show how often each coin's support really held (target hit before stop).

Each entry shows price · distance · chance = how often this coin's price has fallen that far at some point within 26 weeks in its own history.
Estimated dollars of futures positions that would be force-closed if price moves there. Long liquidations sit below price, short liquidations above. Price is often pulled toward the bigger pile nearby, because hitting it triggers forced selling or buying that pushes further (a liquidation cascade). Magnet points to the side with more money within 10%. Binance does not publish real liquidation levels: this is rebuilt from open-interest changes, top-trader long/short ratio and a typical leverage mix, and covers positions opened in the last ~30 days.

Gold Entry Pro v4 — adaptive context + execution + trace

Adaptive scoring across multi-timeframe regime, trend/momentum, structure, strategy ensemble, OCC evidence, order flow, derivatives, BTC/ETH context, relative strength, execution liquidity and exchange events
Power v4 adds context, execution, trace and command-center memory. Regime is now read across 1h/4h/12h/1d; altcoins are compared with BTC and ETH; derivatives distinguish fresh position-building from covering/liquidation; and liquidity uses live spread, book depth and estimated $10k slippage. Gold signals are automatically paper-tracked in browser storage with entry, stop, target, MFE/MAE and lifecycle state. The score remains a research ranking, not a probability or investment recommendation.
Press Scan. Fifty coins takes about half a minute.
Core candles remain closed-bar only. Power v4 additionally reads multi-timeframe regimes, BTC/ETH market context, relative strength, futures OI/funding/top-trader positioning and live book execution conditions. Paper records are stored locally in the browser and are updated only when the scanner runs; they are a research journal, not a broker account or guaranteed fill simulator. Exchange-event risk remains directional. Validate with walk-forward and paper testing before treating any score as executable edge.
